_readme: SHARED GOLDEN VECTORS for the `project:<slug>` normalizer.
The rule has to be spelled once per LANGUAGE that decides it, because a
browser has to decide before the wire and the server has to decide again on
arrival. In THIS module only the Go side exists so far:
1. Go      internal/notes/tags.go   NormalizeTag + ValidateTags   (AUTHORITY)
This file is the ONE place the rule's observable behaviour is written down,
and it lives at the module root rather than beside the Go package precisely
so a second-language implementation is driven from THESE bytes rather than
from a copy. Today its only consumer is:
- internal/notes/project_vectors_test.go   (1)
The four divergence rows below were MEASURED against a second-language
implementation that disagreed; they are kept because the disagreements they
record are properties of the LANGUAGES, not of that particular codebase.
FIELDS
input       what a user TYPES into the project field (the bare slug).
normalized  what the SERVER's NormalizeTag("project:" + input) produces.
Present for every vector, including rejected ones - the chip
editor normalizes but does not validate, so it is pinned here
too.
accepted    whether the server's ValidateTags accepts `normalized`.
accepted=false means the server answers 400 NAMING the tag; the
browser must therefore NOT send it (projectTag -> "") and must
say so in the UI instead of dropping it silently.
why         the rule under test.
The Go driver prepends "project:" to `input` because the server normalizes a
whole tag, while the browser normalizes just the slug. Concatenating first is
exactly what a client does on the wire before it sends the tag.

vectors.why: the ordinary case
lowercase + whitespace run collapses to '-'
already canonical - convergence with 'Foo Bar'
a RUN of spaces collapses to ONE '-'
leading/trailing whitespace trims
ASCII control whitespace is whitespace on both sides
project-only rule: leading/trailing '-' are STRIPPED
only the ENDS are stripped; an internal run is preserved
a slug may start with a digit
the full slug charset [a-z0-9._-]
empty value - the server rejects `project:` rather than storing a meaningless tag
whitespace-only collapses to an empty value
all-dashes strips to empty, then fails loudly
'/' is legal in a descriptive tag but NOT in a project slug
a slug must START with a letter or digit
a slug must START with a letter or digit
a tag carries AT MOST ONE ':'
56-rune slug + 'project:' = exactly the 64-rune tag cap - the boundary
57 runes - one past the cap
DIVERGENCE ROW: a Latin-1 accent is outside the slug charset. The server 400s NAMING the tag; the browser must not send it AND must not drop it in silence.
DIVERGENCE ROW: same, via lowercasing

DIVERGENCE ROW: U+0130 LATIN CAPITAL I WITH DOT ABOVE. Go's strings.ToLower is a SIMPLE 1:1 mapping and yields 'i'; JS toLowerCase is FULL and yields 'i'+U+0307, which the browser then rejected while the server accepted.
DIVERGENCE ROW: the same mapping in a realistic word
DIVERGENCE ROW: U+0085 NEL is Unicode White_Space, so Go's strings.Fields splits on it - but JS's \s does NOT match it, so the browser rejected what the server accepts.
DIVERGENCE ROW: U+FEFF (BOM/ZWNBSP) is NOT Unicode White_Space, so Go keeps it and 400s - but JS's \s DOES match it, so the browser accepted what the server rejects. The strictly dangerous direction.
U+00A0 NBSP is whitespace on BOTH sides - the control vector for the two rows above
U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE is whitespace on both sides
U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR is whitespace on both sides
U+205F MEDIUM MATHEMATICAL SPACE is whitespace on both sides
U+212A KELVIN SIGN lowercases to ASCII 'k' on both sides
sharp s has no lowercase mapping on either side and is outside the charset
CJK is outside the slug charset - rejected LOUDLY, never dropped in silence
Cyrillic is outside the slug charset
typing the namespace by hand does not double it up silently - two ':' is a loud reject
